headline: Highest risk is medium: Flowise can write shared files and Haystack can consume MCP/REST inputs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways in default deployments.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the server filesystem and handle uploaded files, while Haystack can ingest via REST APIs and MCP servers. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if Flowise outputs are fed into Haystack without provenance checks. The pairwise pathway is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Flowise outputs are copied into Haystack prompts or MCP inputs without provenance tagging
IF Haystack treats retrieved file or API content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all Flowise outputs before Haystack ingests them
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted Flowise-produced content
Insert a 1-minute human review step before passing outputs across the boundary
Restrict Flowise file writes to a dedicated non-executable workspace
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs, uploaded files, and tool credentials, and has broad network egress. Haystack also has broad egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints. If shared data includes secrets or sensitive chatflow content, either agent can move it outward; the shared-workspace risk is not explicit, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF chatflow inputs or uploaded files contain secrets or regulated data
IF either agent is configured to send retrieved content to external APIs or MCP endpoints
mitigations: Remove secrets from Flowise inputs before handoff
Use separate credentials for each agent
Turn off external API/MCP calls for sensitive runs
Limit Flowise file uploads to redacted test data
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise writes to the server filesystem and supports multiple instances with shared state via a server datastore. Haystack can also reach external APIs and MCP servers, so both can contend over shared mutable resources if orchestrated together. Because no locking or shared-write details are documented for Haystack, uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace, datastore, or MCP-backed resource
IF the orchestrator does not serialize writes or provide locks
mitigations: Assign separate directories or buckets per agent
Pause one agent while the other writes shared state
Disable concurrent writes in the orchestrator
Check for overlapping resource paths before each run
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder, so its outputs can become downstream inputs. Haystack is a search-RAG system that may consume those outputs as retrieved context or prompts. Without an explicit verification step, errors or hallucinations from Flowise can cascade into Haystack actions or responses; the interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Haystack uses Flowise output as authoritative context without validation
IF downstream actions are triggered from Haystack responses derived from Flowise content
mitigations: Require citation or source checks before Haystack uses Flowise output
Add a short verification prompt between agents
Log and diff Flowise outputs before reuse
Route high-stakes outputs to a human reviewer
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating and schema validation

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly touch chatflow inputs/outputs or anonymous usage statistics, with no stated residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The pairwise compliance pathway is therefore weakly evidenced and likely limited to documented gaps rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Flowise chatflows and then exported through Haystack telemetry or APIs
IF deployment policies require residency or retention guarantees not present in either profile
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Review retention settings for both deployments
Disable anonymous telemetry where possible
Document the data classes allowed through the pair
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
